23.description: The city forwarded the Saskatoon Heritage Society's sponsorship request for its 50th anniversary to the Administration's Special Events Committee for review.

chips.text: Approved
Saskatoon Heritage Society receives a Sask Lotteries grant.

6.description: Saskatoon is changing how advisory committees spend discretionary funds. Committees can approve spending up to $2,000, but larger amounts or budget reallocations need Standing Policy Committee approval.

chips.text: Advisory committees must now submit annual budgets to City Council.
Administration commits to adjusting the new process based on committee feedback.

22.description: Saskatoon advisory committees now have a $2,000 spending limit and must get approval for larger expenses. They also need to submit annual budgets by October 1 for Council review.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor clarified how the $2,000 spending limit interacts with the overall budget.
City advisory committees are directly impacted by new budget rules.
Staff committed to providing administrative support and adjusting processes based on feedback.

20.description: Saskatoon is prioritizing four key items for its Heritage Conservation Program, including a property tax mechanism and policy revisions, to better support heritage property owners.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor Randy highlighted current grants are inaccessible for non-designated heritage properties.
Heritage property owners could see annual property tax reductions.
Administration aims to implement a property tax mechanism by year-end.

8.description: The Committee will review five years of heritage property data for residential and commercial designations, aiming to establish standardized annual reporting.

chips.text: Approved
Owners of residential and commercial heritage properties
Establishes standardized annual data summary for heritage properties
Administration will provide 5 years of heritage data by June meeting

9.description: Saskatoon's Civic Heritage Policy is being reviewed to improve clarity, update language, and address financial aspects, making it more accessible for property owners and the public.

chips.text: Received as information
Policy language is difficult to digest and not approachable for property owners.
Whether the city wants to pursue including intangible cultural heritage is unclear.
Inclusion of intangible heritage could affect Indigenous and immigrant communities.
Committee members will provide suggested edits to the policy for the May meeting.

12.description: The Municipal Heritage Advisory Committee Chair updated on their 2026 Work Plan and discussed a motion to adjust agenda procedures for volunteer speakers at council meetings.

chips.text: Received as information
Councillor Donauer moved to adjust agenda procedures for volunteer speakers.
Volunteer committee chairs affected by agenda delays.
How to engage more youth in heritage activities?
